links.outcome: Factual correctness and information quality of ChatGPT vs physician responses to drug queries, blinded raters
links.effect: All three evaluators rated physician responses higher in information quality and preferred them; factually wrong information was detected more frequently in chatbot responses than physician responses.
links.quote: All evaluators detected factually wrong information more frequently in chatbot-generated responses than in physician-generated responses.

links.outcome: ChatGPT compared against physicians on the same real-world pharmacotherapy queries
links.effect: ChatGPT responses were substantially inferior to physician-generated responses for information quality and factual correctness; all three evaluators preferred physician answers.
links.quote: ChatGPT's responses to real-world pharmacotherapeutic queries were substantially inferior compared to conventional physician-generated responses with regard to quality of information and factual correctness.

screen.reason: Evaluated ChatGPT-3.5 against physician responses for 70 real-world pharmacotherapeutic queries without testing a deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
